title: Act of Settlement (1701)
key_facts: Act of Parliament determining succession to the English (later British) throne
Ensured a Protestant succession, passing the crown to the House of Hanover if William III and Anne had no surviving heirs
Further limited monarchical power and strengthened parliamentary constitutionalism
causes: Succession uncertainty following the Glorious Revolution and childless monarchs
Desire to entrench the Protestant succession and avoid dynastic instability
Ongoing constitutional settlement begun by the Bill of Rights (1689)
outcome: Secured the Hanoverian succession (George I in 1714)
Reinforced parliamentary sovereignty over succession and governance
Shaped the development of the British constitutional monarchy

figures.name: Princess Sophia of Hanover
figures.role: Designated heir presumptive under the Act

impacts: Stabilized succession and fostered political continuity
Facilitated the emergence of cabinet government and party politics
Influenced constitutional thinking across the Atlantic world
